text: In first-order logic, which of the following is a *term* (as opposed to a formula)?
choices: f(x, c), where f is a binary function symbol and c a constant
R(x, y), where R is a binary relation symbol
explanation: Terms are variables, constants, and function symbols applied to terms, so f(x, c) is a term (it names an object). R(x, y) is an atomic FORMULA (it denotes a truth value), and ∀xP(x) and P(x)→Q(x) are formulas. Terms name objects; formulas make claims.
